scenes.tts: How does the nose keep a thousand receptor types on separate lines?
scenes.visual: An olfactory epithelium full of neurons in many colours. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: How does the nose keep a thousand receptor types on separate lines?

scenes.tts: Most mature olfactory neurons in a mouse express one receptor gene at high abundance. That receptor can still bind many odorants.
scenes.visual: One neuron highlighted, one receptor gene lit in its nucleus. Label: most mature mouse neurons.
scenes.narration: Most mature olfactory neurons in a mouse express one receptor gene at high abundance. That receptor can still bind many odorants.

scenes.tts: So all the neurons with one receptor form one line.
scenes.visual: All neurons of one colour light up together. Label: one line.
scenes.narration: So all the neurons with one receptor form one line.

scenes.tts: Where do their axons go? Mombaerts and colleagues made one receptor's neurons fill their axons with a marker.
scenes.visual: Animated schematic, labelled as such: neurons expressing one receptor fill with a blue marker. Caption: Mombaerts and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: Where do their axons go? Mombaerts and colleagues made one receptor's neurons fill their axons with a marker.

scenes.tts: The labelled cells were scattered across the epithelium. Their axons gathered and ended in two fixed glomeruli in each bulb.
scenes.visual: Blue cell bodies scattered across the epithelium; their axons gather and end in two glomeruli in each olfactory bulb.
scenes.narration: The labelled cells were scattered across the epithelium. Their axons gathered and ended in two fixed glomeruli in each bulb.

scenes.tts: Each glomerulus collects mainly from neurons with one receptor type.
scenes.visual: The bulb surface tiled with glomeruli, each a different colour. Label: about 1,800 glomeruli per mouse bulb.
scenes.caption: Each glomerulus collects mainly from neurons with one receptor type.
scenes.narration: Each glomerulus collects mainly from neurons with one receptor type.

scenes.tts: So the glomerular layer is largely a map of lines.
scenes.visual: Label on the bulb: a map of lines; receptor identity becomes position.
scenes.narration: So the glomerular layer is largely a map of lines.

scenes.tts: What does each line detect? Malnic and colleagues imaged single mouse neurons as odorants were applied.
scenes.visual: Dissociated neurons glowing as odorants are applied. Caption: Malnic, Hirono, Sato and Buck, 1999.
scenes.narration: What does each line detect? Malnic and colleagues imaged single mouse neurons as odorants were applied.

scenes.tts: Then they identified the receptor in each responding cell.
scenes.visual: Responding cells are picked out; each is tagged with its receptor name.
scenes.narration: Then they identified the receptor in each responding cell.

scenes.tts: One receptor recognized several odorants. One odorant was recognized by several receptors.
scenes.visual: A grid builds: receptors down the side, odorants across the top, filled squares where cells responded.
scenes.narration: One receptor recognized several odorants. One odorant was recognized by several receptors.

scenes.tts: And concentration could change which receptors an odorant activated. Together, these make a combinatorial code.
scenes.visual: One column of the grid gains a filled square as its concentration rises. Label: combinatorial code.
scenes.narration: And concentration could change which receptors an odorant activated. Together, these make a combinatorial code.

scenes.tts: Now practise reading such a code. This matrix is invented for illustration.
scenes.visual: A new four-by-four grid, captioned: invented for illustration.
scenes.narration: Now practise reading such a code. This matrix is invented for illustration.

scenes.tts: Four receptors, A to D, each simply on or off.
scenes.visual: Grid columns labelled A, B, C, D. Small note: real responses are graded and noisy.
scenes.narration: Four receptors, A to D, each simply on or off.

scenes.tts: Odorant one turns on A and B. Odorant two, B and C. Odorant three, A, B and C. Odorant four, D alone.
scenes.visual: Rows fill in: 1 = A, B; 2 = B, C; 3 = A, B, C; 4 = D.
scenes.narration: Odorant one turns on A and B. Odorant two, B and C. Odorant three, A, B and C. Odorant four, D alone.

scenes.tts: Remove receptor A. Which two odorants now give the same pattern?
scenes.visual: Column A greys out. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Remove receptor A. Which two odorants now give the same pattern?

scenes.tts: Odorants two and three. Both now read B and C, so the model predicts they cannot be told apart.
scenes.visual: Rows 2 and 3 highlight; both show B, C. Label: same pattern.
scenes.narration: Odorants two and three. Both now read B and C, so the model predicts they cannot be told apart.

scenes.tts: Now put receptor A back, and raise odorant one to tenfold concentration. Receptor C has a lower affinity for it, so it responds only at the higher concentration.
scenes.visual: Column A returns, so all four receptors are back. Then a concentration slider beside odorant 1 rises to 10x. Receptor C labelled lower affinity.
scenes.narration: Now put receptor A back, and raise odorant one to tenfold concentration. Receptor C has a lower affinity for it, so it responds only at the higher concentration.

scenes.tts: What happens to odorant one's pattern?
scenes.visual: Odorant 1's row with a question mark over column C.
scenes.narration: What happens to odorant one's pattern?

scenes.tts: C is recruited. Odorant one now reads A, B and C, the pattern of odorant three.
scenes.visual: Square C in row 1 lights faintly, then fully. Rows 1 and 3 now match.
scenes.narration: C is recruited. Odorant one now reads A, B and C, the pattern of odorant three.

scenes.tts: The model predicts it could be mistaken for odorant three. Quality can change with concentration.
scenes.visual: Label: quality can change with concentration.
scenes.narration: The model predicts it could be mistaken for odorant three. Quality can change with concentration.

scenes.tts: This toy counts patterns, not smells. What a mouse can tell apart needs a behavioural test.
scenes.visual: Card: toy model, not a count of smells; behaviour must be tested.
scenes.narration: This toy counts patterns, not smells. What a mouse can tell apart needs a behavioural test.

scenes.tts: Smell keeps its lines apart. So an odour is read as a pattern across many of them.
scenes.visual: Final card: most mature neurons, one receptor gene; about two glomeruli per receptor type per bulb; an odour is a pattern across lines.
scenes.narration: Smell keeps its lines apart. So an odour is read as a pattern across many of them.
